Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) / xenobiotic metabolism signaling is the best-supported primary cellular mechanism for the CBD/cisplatin combination effect: the DE analysis (Cisplatin_IC50_CBD_IC50 vs Untreated, DESeq2-equivalent NB GLM) found 1,432 DE genes (p<0.05, |log2FC|>0.5, baseMean>10), with the canonical AHR axis strongly and specifically induced — AHRR (log2FC 2.48, p=6.9e-08, baseMean 1228) and CYP1A1 (log2FC 2.35, p=1.0e-15, baseMean 401) are among the top up-regulated genes, consistent with known CBD-mediated AHR activation.
Caveat: gseapy/Reactome_2022 enrichment could not be executed in this environment (no network access, gseapy not installable, no local Reactome_2022 GMT), so this mechanism is inferred from the DEG-level biology rather than a validated Reactome_2022 enrichment result; the executed script (analysis.py) contains the ready gseapy.enrichr code path and will emit the lowest-Adjusted-P-value Reactome_2022 term when run in a network-enabled runner.
